name: ST25DV16K-JFR6D3
title: Dynamic NFC/RFID tag with I2C, 4/16/64-Kbit EEPROM and fast transfer mailbox
summary: A dual-interface EEPROM: a contactless ISO/IEC 15693 (NFC Forum Type 5) tag powered from a 13.56 MHz reader field, and a 1 MHz I2C slave powered from VCC at 1.8 V to 5.5 V. ST25DV04K, ST25DV16K and ST25DV64K hold 512, 2048 and 8192 bytes of user EEPROM, split into up to four areas each with its own RF and I2C read/write protection under 64-bit passwords. A 256-byte volatile mailbox passes messages between the reader and the I2C host, a GPO pin flags RF events to the host, and a V_EH pin hands out unregulated harvested power. The -IE parts (8-pin) have an open-drain GPO; the -JF parts (12-pin and WLCSP10) have a push-pull GPO on its own VDCG supply and an LPD input that powers the device down. ST25DV04K-JFR6D3 is the 4-Kbit -JF part in UFDFPN12, grade 6 (-40 °C to 85 °C), with 28.5 pF internal tuning capacitance.

circuits.title: I2C bus with pull-up Rbus and bus capacitance Cbus
circuits.description: An I2C master and the tag share SCL and SDA, both powered from VCC. Rbus pulls SDA up to VCC and Cbus stands for the total parasitic capacitance of the line to ground. Rbus is read off the Rbus-versus-Cbus graph so that Rbus × Cbus stays under 150 ns at 1 MHz; 4 kΩ with 30 pF gives 120 ns. An SCL pull-up is needed only when the master drives SCL open-drain.

operation.text: The tag has two ways in. Over RF it behaves as an ISO/IEC 15693 / NFC Forum Type 5 tag powered by the reader's field and reads or writes 4-byte blocks; over I2C it is a slave at device type 1010b powered from VCC and addresses single bytes. User EEPROM is 512, 2048 or 8192 bytes (128, 512 or 2048 blocks). Besides it there are dynamic (volatile) registers, the 256-byte mailbox and a system configuration area of static EEPROM registers, the UID, AFI, DSFID and five 64-bit passwords.

The device select byte is 1010 E2 1 1 RW. E2 is not a pin: E2 = 0 selects user memory, dynamic registers (2000h-2007h) and mailbox (2008h-2107h); E2 = 1 selects the system area (0000h-0023h, I2C password at 0900h). Two address bytes follow, MSB first. Reads stop at area borders and at the end of memory, returning FFh beyond; there is no roll-over.

A Stop right after the acknowledge of the last byte starts the internal write. Up to 256 bytes go in one sequential write, all in the same area. EEPROM is programmed in 4-byte pages, tW each; mailbox and dynamic register writes complete at the acknowledge with no write time. A refused byte (protected area, read-only register, closed session, area border crossed, mailbox busy or not first byte) is not acknowledged and the whole sequence writes nothing. While the write runs the device ignores the bus; polling with a device select until it acknowledges ends the wait as soon as programming is done.

operation.topic: EEPROM writes need the mailbox off
operation.text: Every EEPROM write, from I2C or RF, passes through the 256-byte mailbox buffer, so fast transfer mode must be off (MB_EN = 0) first. Otherwise I2C gets no acknowledge, RF gets error 0Fh, and nothing is programmed. The same holds for the I2C Write Password command.

If the first SCL rising edge after a Start comes later than tSTART_OUT (35 ms min), or SCL stays high or low past tCHCL or tCLCH (25 ms), the I2C logic resets and waits for the next Start. This stops a stuck bus from locking out RF.

VCC must rise no faster than 1 V/µs. A power-on reset holds the I2C side off until VCC passes its threshold, below the 1.8 V minimum; access must then wait for VCC within range and the boot time tboot (0.6 ms max). On parts with LPD the boot starts only once LPD is low. Below the threshold on the way down the device stops answering and its address counter resets. A 10 nF to 100 nF decoupling capacitor near the VCC and VSS pins keeps the supply steady; it must stay valid through each instruction and write cycle.

The reader must hold the field unmodulated for the boot time before the tag accepts commands (tBootRF 0.6 ms typ, first data within 1 ms of the minimum field). Switching the field fully off for at least tRF_OFF (2 ms) resets the RF side.

On the 12-pin and 10-ball (-JF) parts, LPD high shuts the internal 1.8 V regulator and supply current drops below 1 µA (ICC1 0.84 µA typ at 1.8 V). The regulator then needs about 100 µs to start, added to the boot time. LPD has an internal pull-down and presents no more than 5 kΩ when driven high.

With MB_MODE = 1, MB_EN = 1 and VCC present, either side can drop a message of up to 256 bytes into the free mailbox. RF writes it with (Fast) Write Message, I2C writes from 2008h. The device sets RF_PUT_MSG or HOST_PUT_MSG and the length minus one in MB_LEN_Dyn; the mailbox is then locked to new writes until the other side has read the message to its last byte, or the MB_WDG watchdog expires (setting HOST_MISS_MSG or RF_MISS_MSG). Data stay in the buffer until fast transfer mode is turned off. The host can learn of an RF message by GPO (RF_PUT_MSG) or by polling MB_CTRL_Dyn; the reader polls MB_CTRL_Dyn. First request is served first. I2C runs at up to 1 Mbit/s and RF reads at up to 53 kbit/s.

GPO tells the I2C host about RF events. Enabled in the GPO register (and its live copy GPO_CTRL_Dyn): RF_USER (level set/reset by Manage GPO), RF_ACTIVITY (active from command EOF to response EOF), RF_INTERRUPT (pulse on Manage GPO), FIELD_CHANGE (pulse when the field appears or goes; on loss only if VCC is present), RF_PUT_MSG and RF_GET_MSG (pulse when RF has written or fully read a mailbox message), RF_WRITE (pulse after an EEPROM write). Pulses last IT_TIME. Factory setting: GPO_EN and FIELD_CHANGE on. On -IE parts the active state is low (open drain released otherwise); on -JF parts it is high, driven from VDCG. IT_STS_Dyn records every event, even with GPO output off, and clears when read.

GPO works only while the RF field is on and, for -IE, its pull-up is powered or, for -JF, VDCG is powered. Without VCC, or in low-power mode, all events still reach GPO except the field-loss pulse, so GPO can wake a sleeping host. When the field goes, GPO returns to idle and IT_STS_Dyn keeps its contents until read or VCC is removed.

V_EH supplies a few microwatts of unregulated power from the reader field when harvesting is on and the field leaves power to spare; otherwise V_EH is high impedance. EH_MODE = 0 turns harvesting on at every boot; EH_MODE = 1 (factory) leaves it off until EH_EN is set in EH_CTRL_Dyn. No power is delivered during boot. RF communication is not guaranteed while V_EH delivers power, and RF traffic can interrupt harvesting. Harvesting works in RF sleep, RF disable and low-power mode.

RF_MNGT (static) and RF_MNGT_Dyn (live copy, I2C only) set three RF modes: normal (both bits 0); RF disable (RF_DISABLE = 1): commands are decoded but answered with 0Fh and Inventory is ignored; RF sleep (RF_SLEEP = 1): the RF side is silent and draws least.

The first interface to start a transaction owns the device. While RF is busy, I2C commands are not acknowledged. While I2C is busy, Inventory, Stay Quiet and addressed commands get no reply and other RF commands get 0Fh. An I2C transaction ends at Stop, at the end of EEPROM programming, on error, on timeout or at VCC loss; an RF transaction ends at the response EOF, the request EOF when there is no answer, or field loss.

User memory has up to four areas set by ENDA1-ENDA3; Area 1 starts at 0, is at least 8 blocks and is always readable. Over RF each area picks one of three RF passwords (RFAiSS) and a read/write rule; over I2C one I2C password and the I2CSS register cover all areas. RF blocks 0 and 1 (I2C bytes 0000h-0007h) can be write-locked on their own: from RF permanently with Lock Block, from I2C reversibly through LOCK_CCFILE. Static configuration is write-protected by RF password 0 and by the I2C password; LOCK_CFG = 1 stops all RF configuration writes and only I2C can clear it. AFI and DSFID locks are permanent. All passwords are 64-bit, 00h from the factory. RF and I2C sessions are independent.

Each ENDAi must satisfy ENDAi-1 < ENDAi ≤ ENDAi+1 = end of memory, or RF returns 0Fh and I2C gives no acknowledge. To change sizes, first set ENDA3 and then ENDA2 to the end of memory (skipping any already there), then write ENDA1, ENDA2, ENDA3 in that order. Changing area sizes leaves RFAiSS and I2CSS untouched.

RF: Present Password with number 1-3 opens an RF user session, with number 0 the configuration session; a different number or a wrong password closes it, as does leaving the field; a new session closes the previous one. A password is changed by presenting it and then sending Write Password with the same number. I2C: the Present Password sequence (address 0900h, 8 bytes, validation code 09h, the 8 bytes again) opens the session if the two copies match and agree with I2C_PWD, and I2C_SSO_Dyn shows the result; a wrong password or VCC loss closes it. Write Password uses validation code 07h and needs the session open. Removing VCC during an RF password write can corrupt it, so the reader should check VCC_ON first.

Reader to tag: 10 % or 100 % ASK, 1.6 kbit/s (1 out of 256) or 26 kbit/s (1 out of 4). Tag to reader: load modulation, Manchester coded on one subcarrier (423 kHz) or two (423/484 kHz), 6.6 kbit/s low or 26 kbit/s high data rate; the Fast commands answer at 53 kbit/s on one subcarrier. The tag has Power-off, Ready, Quiet and Selected states and answers non-addressed, addressed (UID) and select-mode requests. Frames run LSB first with a 16-bit CRC.
The 64-bit read-only UID is E0h, the ST manufacturer code 02h, an 8-bit product code and a 48-bit serial number. It is used in anticollision and addressed commands.
AC0 and AC1 take only an external coil, with no other DC or AC path on them. The internal tuning capacitance is 28.5 pF typ and is the reference value for antenna design.
